title: Go toolchain pinned
description: Go is installed on the dev machine (go1.26.8 linux/amd64). Pin the same version in go.mod's go directive and in the CI workflow image so local and CI builds match. Record the version in README.
acceptance_criteria: go version prints go1.26.8; go.mod go directive is 1.26.8; CI uses the identical version; README states the version and how to check it

title: Bootstrap Go module and CLI skeleton
description: Create go.mod (module github.com/josepalala-dev/gitgud), cmd/gitgud/main.go and empty packages internal/git, internal/workflow, internal/events, internal/cli, internal/state. Add --version flag.
acceptance_criteria: go build ./... succeeds; go vet ./... clean; gitgud --version prints a version string; go.mod has no unpinned or floating dependencies

title: Native git runner
description: internal/git executes the git binary via exec.CommandContext with argument slices only (no shell string). Captures stdout, stderr and exit code into a typed error that includes the command line and stderr.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test runs git rev-parse in a temp repo; a failing command returns an error containing the argv and stderr; no call site passes a shell string

title: Repository guard
description: Detect repo root and git common dir (git rev-parse --git-common-dir so worktrees work). Detect current branch. Refuse with a named error when not inside a repo or when HEAD is detached.
acceptance_criteria: Outside a repo returns ErrNotRepo; detached HEAD returns ErrDetachedHead; inside a worktree the state dir resolves to the common .git dir

title: Slug generator
description: internal/workflow Slugify turns a free-text description into a branch-safe slug: lowercase ASCII, non-alphanumerics become single hyphens, trimmed, capped at 40 chars without a trailing hyphen. Deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Table test: 'readline from user' -> 'readline-from-user'; 'Fix -- Login!!  bug' -> 'fix-login-bug'; empty or symbol-only input returns ErrEmptySlug; output never exceeds 40 chars

title: Branch policy table
description: internal/workflow encodes allowed parents: feature from develop or epic; fix from develop or epic; epic from develop only; release from develop, integrating into main then develop. Validates a requested parent against the table.
acceptance_criteria: Test: feature with parent main is rejected; epic with parent develop accepted; release targets are main and develop; unknown type returns a named error

title: Branch state file in .git
description: Persist branch metadata to <git-common-dir>/gitgud/state.json: schema_version, and per branch: type, parent, slug, created_at, base_sha, status (open or finished). Used for parent lookup only; the journal is the history record. Writes are atomic (temp file then rename). Missing file reads as empty state.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip test equals input; missing file reads as empty state; a simulated crash mid-write leaves the previous file intact; file is valid JSON with schema_version 1.0

title: Operation ID generation
description: Generate sortable unique operation IDs (op_ prefix plus time-ordered random suffix). Used as the operation_id in JSON results and journal records, and as a comparator anchor.
acceptance_criteria: IDs are unique over 10000 generations in a test; IDs sort by creation time; same ID appears in result and journal for one operation

title: Per-branch JSONL commit journal
description: Append one JSON object per line to <git-common-dir>/gitgud/journal/<branch>.jsonl, where / in the branch name becomes __ (feature/login -> feature__login.jsonl). Each record: seq (per-file increasing integer), ts (RFC 3339 UTC), op_id, event, branch, commit (full 40-char SHA), parents (full SHAs), subject, type (Conventional Commit type parsed from subject, or null), source, target. Append-only; GitHero-flow never truncates or rewrites a journal. Records are flat so jq can read them without a schema.
acceptance_criteria: Two appends produce seq 1 and 2; every line parses as JSON; commit is always 40 hex chars; files only grow; a branch with / in its name maps to the expected file

title: Dirty-tree and integrity guards
description: Before any checkout, merge or branch creation: refuse when the working tree has uncommitted changes, including untracked files, or a merge is already in progress. Refuse to operate on a branch missing from state.json unless it is develop or main.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: dirty tree blocks new, sync and finish with status refused; untracked file blocks the same operations; unrecorded feature branch cannot be finished; merge in progress blocks all three

title: Commit capture into the journal
description: After any GitHero-flow operation that moves a branch tip (new, sync, finish), run git rev-list <old>..<new> and append one journal record per new commit, oldest first. Add gitgud record to capture commits made with plain git since the last journaled SHA on the current branch, so the journal stays complete without requiring GitHero-flow to make the commits.
acceptance_criteria: After a feature gets two plain-git commits, gitgud record appends exactly those two, in order; running gitgud record again appends nothing; a gitgud new that makes no commits appends an event record with no commit field

title: gitgud init
description: Ensure develop and main exist (create develop from main, or main from the current HEAD, when missing). Create the GitHero-flow state and journal directories and an empty state.json if absent. Idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: Running twice produces no change on second run; missing develop is created from main; output reports which branches were created

title: gitgud new feature|fix|epic
description: Interactive creation: when no description is given, prompt 'What does this <type> do?' on stdin; with a quoted description argument skip the prompt. Slugify the description, branch from develop (or from --parent when allowed by policy) using git checkout -b, record type/parent/base_sha in state, append a branch.created journal event, and leave the new branch checked out. Branch names: feature/<slug>, fix/<slug>, epic/<slug>.
acceptance_criteria: gitgud new fix (typing 'readline from user') creates and checks out fix/readline-from-user from develop; state.json records type fix and parent develop; journal file fix__readline-from-user.jsonl gets a branch.created record; uncommitted or untracked changes refuse before any branch is created; existing branch name is refused with a named error

title: gitgud new release <version>
description: Create release/<version> from develop via checkout -b and record it in state and the journal. Version prompt when omitted; validate MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format.
acceptance_criteria: release/1.4.0 created from develop; 1.4 or v1.4.0 rejected with named error; state.json records type release and parent develop

title: gitgud sync
description: Bring the parent branch into the current branch with git merge --no-ff <parent>. Never rebases and never fast-forwards. Refuses on dirty tree; captures new commits into the journal (GG-026) and records a sync event.
acceptance_criteria: Test: after parent gains a commit, sync creates a merge commit with two parents; journal gains the merge commit record; no rebase or --ff-only invocation exists in code; dirty tree refused

title: gitgud finish for feature and fix
description: Merge the current feature or fix branch into its recorded parent with git merge --no-ff, mark it finished in state, and append a branch.finished journal event with the merge commit SHA. Branch is kept by default; --delete removes it after success.
acceptance_criteria: Test: merge commit on parent has the feature tip as second parent; state marks branch finished; journal has branch.finished with merge commit; no history rewrite; JSON reports target and after.merge_commit

title: gitgud finish for epic
description: Merge an epic into develop with --no-ff. Refuses while any recorded child feature or fix is still open.
acceptance_criteria: Open child feature blocks finish with status refused and next_actions listing it; after children finish, epic merges into develop with merge-no-ff strategy

title: gitgud finish for release
description: Merge release/<version> into main with --no-ff, create an annotated tag v<version>, then merge the same release into develop with --no-ff. Mark finished in state and journal the tag and both merge SHAs.
acceptance_criteria: Tag v<version> exists on main after finish; develop contains a merge of the release; both merges have the release tip as second parent; journal records both merge SHAs and the tag; no rebase used

title: Conflict handling
description: When git merge stops with conflicts, do not abort or reset. Leave the merge in progress, append a merge.conflict journal event with the file list, and return status conflict with next_actions telling the developer to resolve, commit, then run gitgud record.
acceptance_criteria: Test with a forced conflict: status is conflict, conflicted files listed, merge still in progress (MERGE_HEAD present), journal has merge.conflict, no abort performed

title: gitgud status
description: Report current branch, type, parent, ahead/behind counts against parent, open children (for epics), journal record count, and whether a merge is in progress. Supports --json.
acceptance_criteria: Human and JSON output agree; on an unrecorded branch status says so; ahead/behind matches git rev-list counts in test

title: gitgud log (raw JSONL for jq)
description: Print the branch journal to stdout as raw JSONL, one record per line, oldest first, so it pipes straight into jq. Default branch is the current one; --branch <name> selects another. --limit N prints the last N lines. Malformed lines are passed through unchanged and reported on stderr.
acceptance_criteria: gitgud log | jq -c . succeeds on a journal fixture; --limit 2 prints exactly the last 2 lines; a corrupted line is printed as-is and a warning goes to stderr; no output is reformatted

title: gitgud compare <from> <to>
description: Given two anchors, each an op_id or a full commit SHA found in any branch journal, list every journal record strictly after <from> up to and including <to>, ordered by ts then seq across all branch journals. Error with a named error if an anchor is not found or <to> precedes <from>. Also supports --branch to restrict to one journal.
acceptance_criteria: Test across two branch journals: compare returns the records in order; unknown anchor returns ErrAnchorNotFound; reversed anchors return ErrRange; same anchor twice returns an empty list

title: gitgud changelog --from <id> --to <id>
description: Run the comparator and group the resulting commits by Conventional Commit type (feat, fix, refactor, docs, and so on, with an other group for null). Output as JSON by default and as Markdown with --format md. Only commit records are included, not events.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture with feat, fix and one untyped commit produces three groups in the expected order; --format md emits a Markdown list; events do not appear in output

title: Porcelain JSON result envelope
description: Every mutating command with --json prints one object: schema_version, operation_id, operation, status (completed, refused, conflict, failed), source, target, strategy, before, after, history_rewritten (always false), next_actions. Human output is the default.
acceptance_criteria: Schema test for each command; history_rewritten is false in every case; failed status includes error message; JSON goes to stdout only and logs to stderr

title: Integration test harness
description: Go tests that create a temp repo, run gitgud init, new feature under an epic, plain-git commits, record, finish feature, finish release, then read the journal back with gitgud log. Assert the branch graph, state.json and every journal file after each step.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./... passes; scenario covers feature -> finish -> release finish; test does not touch the real repo; runs under 30 seconds

title: Safety audit test
description: Test that scans the source for forbidden git subcommands (rebase, merge --ff-only, reset --hard, push, force flags) and fails if any appear outside the test files.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails when a forbidden string is injected into a temporary copy of a source file; passes on the real tree

title: README and journal format doc
description: README covers install, init, new, record, finish, log, and the branch model table. docs/journal-format.md documents the journal record fields and event names with one example. Add a jq cookbook section: list commits in a branch, filter by type, show the merge SHA for each finished branch, and count records per event.
acceptance_criteria: Every command in the README exists in --help output; every event name in the code appears in docs/journal-format.md; every field in a journal record appears in the doc; each jq recipe runs against a fixture and gives the documented output

title: CI gates
description: Add a CI workflow running gofmt check, go vet, go test ./... and go build ./cmd/gitgud on push and pull request, using the Go version from GG-000.
acceptance_criteria: Workflow file present; all four steps pass locally with the same commands; no step installs or pushes anything

title: Public repository hygiene
description: The repo will be public. Add LICENSE (MIT, owner confirmed), .gitignore (bin/, *.test, .DS_Store, editor files), SECURITY.md with a private reporting channel, and CONTRIBUTING.md describing Conventional Commits and the no-rebase/no-ff rule. Scan history for secrets before the first push.
acceptance_criteria: LICENSE present with the MIT license text naming the owner; .gitignore excludes bin/ and .tools/ and gitignores nothing under .git; SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md exist; a secret scan (for example gitleaks) reports no findings on the full history before publishing
